title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
creator: Stanley Kubrick
invention: HAL 9000, tablet newspads, a video-phone booth in orbit, and a Pan Am shuttle to the Moon
summary: REPLACE: short summary in your own words.

tech.name: Picturephone
tech.description: Demonstrated at the 1964 New York World's Fair, four years before the film. Bell Labs engineers then designed the film's video-phone booth, Bell System logo included.

references.title: A. Michael Noll, "First-Hand: Bell Labs and 2001: A Space Odyssey," ETHW

tech.name: First Moon Flights Club
tech.description: A waiting list for commercial Moon flights, started the year the film showed a Pan Am "Space Clipper". Pan Am printed 100,000 membership cards before closing the list in 1971.

references.title: Robert E. Dallos, Los Angeles Times
Smithsonian: "I Was a Card-Carrying Member of the First Moon Flights Club"

tech.name: NewsPAD
tech.description: An EU-funded portable multimedia tablet, meant as an electronic newspaper. It shares its name with the "newspad" in Clarke's novel, but the project's own documents don't mention 2001.

references.title: Acorn RISC Technologies, NewsPAD datasheet DS003

tech.name: iPad
tech.description: Apple never credited the film. In 2011 Samsung cited its tablets as prior art against Apple's iPad design patent; the court rejected the argument in 2012.

references.title: Ned Potter, "Apple iPad vs Samsung Galaxy: Stanley Kubrick Showed Tablet in '2001: A Space Odyssey'," ABC News
Mikey Campbell, "Judge denies Samsung's '2001: A Space Odyssey,' Fidler Tablet arguments," AppleInsider

tech.name: Siri
tech.description: Apple's voice assistant. Asked to "open the pod bay doors", it answers with HAL's line: an easter egg that references the film rather than claiming inspiration from it.

references.title: Melanie Jones, "iPhone 4S Siri Goes '2001: Space Odyssey'," International Business Times

tech.name: CASE (Cognitive Architecture for Space Agents)
tech.description: An AI that ran a simulated planetary base for about four hours: power, oxygen, CO₂ removal and rovers. Its developer says HAL 9000 was the model.

references.title: Pete Bonasso, "CASE: A HAL 9000 for 2021," Science Robotics 3(24)
Charles Q. Choi, "This HAL 9000-Inspired AI Simulation Kept Its Virtual Astronauts Alive," Space.com
